title: Microscope Slides in Motion — source and archive registry supplement 04

records.collection: Histothèque — Philippe Van Tieghem and pupils core collection
records.holdings: The MNHN Histothèque contains more than 67,000 botanical histological sections. Its core historical collection was produced by Philippe Van Tieghem and his pupils from 1875 to 1914 and accounts for roughly one third of the slide holdings. The oldest preparations remain stored flat in purpose-built glazed drawers, while other preparations are kept in grooved boxes.
records.research_use: A major nineteenth-century teaching and research slide archive in which preparations can be tied to botanical anatomy, named researchers, storage systems, and publications. MNHN notes that in some studies the preparations are the only surviving illustrations because no figure or photograph was published.
records.access: On-site collection consultation under MNHN collection-access procedures; the slides are currently described as difficult to access except by direct microscopic examination.

records.type: slide collection + specimen archive + drawings and field notes
records.holdings: The MNHN micropalaeontology collection includes microscope slides with isolated specimens or assemblages, thin sections, cover-glass mounts, and other microscopic preparations. Major historical holdings include the Alcide d'Orbigny foraminifera collection and later specialist collections. Rock samples and sediments associated with type material are preserved alongside archives including original drawings and field notes.
records.research_use: High-value object↔archive route for tracking how microscopic fossil material moved between raw sediment, isolated specimen, slide, figured/type status, drawing, field documentation, and later museum custody.
records.access: Research consultation and loans through the MNHN micropalaeontology collection managers and collections database.

records.institution: McGill University Library — Rare Books and Special Collections
records.collection: Natural History Society of Montreal fonds, including Montreal Microscopical Society series
records.holdings: The fonds contains accounting and administrative records, catalogues of holdings, correspondence, essays and lectures, minutes, reports, newspaper clippings, and publication records. A dedicated Montreal Microscopical Society series covers 1884–1906.
records.research_use: A rare North American society archive for testing slide exchange, purchases, donations, meeting display, collection cataloguing, and the relationship between a microscopical society and a broader natural-history institution.
records.access: Archival description and finding aid online; consultation through McGill Rare Books and Special Collections.

records.date_scope: 1896–1941 with research roots in the late nineteenth century
records.holdings: Adams' fonds documents experiments on mechanical rock deformation through notebooks, notes, photographs and experimental material. The archival description explicitly includes more than 1,000 photographs, glass negatives, and petrographic microscope slides, together with an index-card bibliography and records of equipment and minerals.
records.research_use: Strong late-nineteenth-century petrography route for joining thin-section preparation and polarized-light microscopy to laboratory notebooks, experiment records, apparatus, photographs, and later publication.
records.access: Archival finding aid online; research consultation through McGill University Archives.

records.collection: Paul S. Conger Papers — Thomas Christian and the Diatomists of Richmond manuscript and research files
records.date_scope: archival papers 1913–1979; manuscript reconstructs Richmond microscopy in the 1880s–1890s
records.holdings: Record Unit 7292 contains Conger's notes and unpublished manuscript 'Thomas Christian and the Diatomists of Richmond,' concerning members of the Richmond Microscopical Society and their diatom work in the 1880s and 1890s. The series includes notes on Thomas Christian, quotations, a 'History of Microscopy in Virginia,' clippings, bibliography, and revised manuscript; associated correspondence is cross-referenced in the finding aid.
records.research_use: A secondary archival reconstruction built from earlier correspondence and surviving knowledge of an American microscopical network. Useful for identifying names, exchanges, slide makers, localities, and source trails that can then be checked against nineteenth-century records and surviving objects.
records.access: Smithsonian Institution Archives finding aid online; consultation by advance arrangement.

records.institution: University of Padua — Zoology Museum / University Museums
records.holdings: The surviving Canestrini arachnological material at the University of Padua includes 438 microscope slides of mites as well as spiders, harvestmen, pseudoscorpions, scorpions and other material. University research identifies type material and material contributed by other European arachnologists as part of a modern revision of the collection.
records.research_use: Object-level route into a nineteenth-century European specialist network: labels, type status, contributors, exchange, collection survival, and the later rediscovery/revision of historical microscope-slide material.
records.access: Research through the University of Padua Zoology Museum; an open university-repository publication documents the rediscovery and revision programme.

records.institution: National Museum of Nature and Science, Tokyo — Tsukuba Botanical Collections
records.type: slide collection + photographic plates + digital databases
records.holdings: The Museum's microalgae herbarium reports 21,457 prepared microscope slides in its 2025 holdings, alongside dried and liquid specimens, electron-microscopy material, sketches, photographic plates, and specimen-derived genomic material. Named collections and specialist databases include freshwater diatoms, type specimens, donor literature, sketches, and photographic-plate archives.
records.research_use: East-Asian route for comparing slide cataloguing, named research collections, photographic documentation and digital databases. Nineteenth-century identity must be established at named-subcollection level rather than inferred from the aggregate slide total.
records.access: Collection and database access through the National Museum of Nature and Science, Tsukuba research facilities.

records.institution: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa
records.collection: Natural-history microscope-slide stores and Te Papa Archives
records.date_scope: museum predecessor institutions from 1865; current natural-history stores
records.holdings: Te Papa's Tory Street research facility houses natural-history dry collections including microscope slides and provides research access to specimens. Te Papa Archives preserves institutional public records and historical documents including Sir James Hector's letters, while Collections Online exposes object and provenance records from the museum and its predecessors.
records.research_use: A route from nineteenth-century Colonial Museum administration and Hector correspondence to later natural-history custody and present slide stores. Useful for testing acquisition and collection movement without assuming that current slide holdings automatically descend from nineteenth-century records.
records.access: Natural-history research visits and archive consultation by appointment; Collections Online is publicly searchable.
